title: Tacony-Palmyra Bridge back open after reported cargo ship strike

 Tacony-Palmyra Bridge back open after reported cargo ship strike 
 Pedestrians are still unable to cross. 
 Tacony-Palmyra Bridge back open after reported cargo ship strike WPVI By 6abc Digital Staff , Briana Smith Friday, November 13, 2026 4:15PM Share Follow 6abc on Google PALMYRA, N.J. (WPVI) -- The Tacony-Palmyra Bridge has reopened to vehicular traffic after Burlington County officials believe it was struck by a cargo ship on Thursday.
 The bridge was closed for more than 6 hours.
 However, as of Friday, the pedestrian cross is still closed as crews continue to make repairs.
 Chopper 6 was overhead as crews inspected the bridge. A metal railing and portions of a brick column had minor damage.
 Officials said the drawbridges were open for marine traffic at the time of the incident, which happened around 1 p.m.
 Traffic was snarled in both New Jersey and Philadelphia. What would normally be a two-hour commute home to Northeast Philadelphia for Rebecca Halper turned into five hours.
 Chopper 6 over Tacony-Palmyra Bridge after cargo ship strike 
 "It was unbelievable. By the time we got there, there were so many cars behind us. It was really a lot of traffic," she said.

 Crews remained on site for hours to complete repairs and conduct mechanical tests to ensure the bridge was safe to reopen.
 One man who was fishing at the Frankford boat launch said he witnessed the incident.
 "I'm almost positive I seen the back end hit that thing, and then all of a sudden the bridge ain't closing," the man said.
 The bridge has two lanes open to vehicle traffic only. The third lane remains closed so crews can fix the pedestrian sidewalk.
 However, Halper plans on finding an alternate route in the near future.
 "I don't know if they need a new bridge, but I would be a little nervous right now, a little skeptical. But that's just the way I am," said Halper.
 No injuries have been reported.
 Officials say the cause of the collision is under investigation.
